Rashi on Arakhin 19a:11:1.hebrew: קומתי - משמע כקומתו, ונותן שרביט עב שלא יוכל לכופפו. אם פירש כסף — כסף, ואם זהב — זהב:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:11:1.english: My height - [This] implies [something] like his stature, and he gives a thick rod that cannot be bent. If he specified silver, [he gives] silver; and if gold, [he gives] gold.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:11:2.hebrew: מלא קומתי - לא נתכוין אלא למדת גובה קומתו, ולא לעובי:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:11:2.english: My full height - He intended only the measure of the height of his stature, and not [its] thickness.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:1:1.hebrew: שבזכר ושבנקבה מיבעי ליה - כלישנא דקרא, דכתיב בערכין (ויקרא כז) אם זכר אם נקבה, ולא כתיב בן ובת. אבל יוצא דופן, כוליה בן ובת תנינן:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:1:1.english: "With regard to a male and with regard to a female" it should have [stated] - In accordance with the phrasing of the verse, as it is written regarding valuations (Leviticus 27): "whether male or female," and it is not written "son" and "daughter." But [in the chapter of] Yotze Dofen, we learn "son" and "daughter" throughout.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא - בערכין, דנקבה, כי מזקנא יותר על ששים, קיימא אתילתא — דערך ילדה שלשים שקל, וערך זקנה עשרת שקלים:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:1.english: And what is different - Regarding valuations: that for a female, when she ages beyond sixty [years], she stands at one-third [of her previous valuation] — for the valuation of a young woman is thirty shekels, and the valuation of an elderly woman is ten shekels.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:2.hebrew: ומאי שנא זכר - דכי עבר על ששים לא קאי אתילתא, דבציר ערך זקן טפי מתילתא בערך ילד, דילד חמשים שקלים, וזקן ט"ו שקלים:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:2.english: And what is different [with regard to] a male - That when he passes sixty [years], he does not stand at a third [of his previous valuation], for the valuation of an old man is even less than a third in relation to the valuation of a young man — as [that of] a young [man] is fifty shekels, and [that of] an old [man] is fifteen shekels.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:3.hebrew: פאחא - שבר שאינו אלא למשא. ל"א: פחחא גרסינן — לשון "ערום ועריה", דמתרגמינן לערום "פחיח" בתרגום של נביאים (יחזקאל טז):
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:3.english: Paḥa - A broken [vessel] that is only a burden. Another explanation: We read [the text as] peḥaḥa — an expression of "naked and bare," as we translate [the word for] "naked" as paḥiḥ in the Targum of the Prophets (Ezekiel 16).

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:4.hebrew: סימא - מטמון, שיכולה לטרוח ולעשות מלאכה בזקנותה:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:2:4.english: A treasure - A hidden treasure, for she is able to exert herself and do work in her old age.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:4:1.english: One who says: “My weight is upon me”:

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:4:2.english: Yirmatya - [This is] the name of the woman.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:1.hebrew: משקל ידי עלי - היאך הוא שוקל? אם רוצה מכביד, ואם רוצה מיקל:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:1.english: The weight of my hand [is] upon me - How can he weigh [it]? If he wishes, he makes [it] heavier, and if he wishes, he makes [it] lighter.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:2.english: He fills a barrel with water and inserts it - Into it.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:3.hebrew: עד מרפיקו - אציל, שקורין איישיל"א. וכשמכניסה יוצאין המים, וכשמוציאה נמצאת חסירה:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:3.english: Up to his elbow - [That is,] the armpit, which they call *aisselle*. And when he inserts it, the water spills out, and when he removes it, [the barrel] is found lacking.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:4.hebrew: ושוקל בשר חמור - שמשקל בשר חמור כמשקל בשר אדם, ויהיו באותו בשר גידין ועצמות לפי מה שיש ביד, לפי שאין משקל עצמות וגידים שוה למשקל בשר. ונותן לתוכה עד שתתמלא — דהשתא איכא נפח כשיעור ידו — וכפי אותו משקל יתן:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:5:4.english: And he weighs donkey flesh - For the weight of donkey flesh is like the weight of human flesh; and there must be in that flesh sinews and bones according to what is in the arm, because the weight of bones and sinews is not equal to the weight of flesh. And he places [it] into [the barrel] until it is filled — for now there is a volume equivalent to the measure of his arm — and according to that weight he shall give.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:6:1.hebrew: נפשיה בכל דהו - כל מה שהוא רוצה לשקול, ישקול:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:6:1.english: [He exempts] himself with anything - Whatever he wants to weigh, he may weigh.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:7:2.english: In a place where they weigh pitch - Where they sell pitch by weight.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:8:2.english: [They] throw [in] two [or] three - As is the practice of merchants.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:8:3.english: [The] weight is nullified - And it turns out that they are not sold by weight.

Rashi on Arakhin 19a:9:1.hebrew: מעשה לסתור - קתני רישא: אם כסף כסף כו', ואוקימנא דקאתא לאשמועינן דאי לא פריש — פטר נפשיה בכל דהו. והדר תני באמה של ירמטיא, שאמרה משקל בתי סתם עלי, ושקלתה בזהב:
Rashi on Arakhin 19a:9:1.english: An incident to contradict?! - The first clause [of the mishna] teaches: "If silver, silver," etc., and we established that it comes to teach us that if he did not specify, he may exempt himself with anything. And then [the mishna] teaches [the incident] involving the mother of Yirmatya, who said, without specifying: "The weight of my daughter is upon me," and she weighed her in gold.

Tosafot on Arakhin 19a:4:1.english: One who says: “My weight is upon me”:

Tosafot on Arakhin 19a:5:1.hebrew: מרפיקו - פי' רש"י: אציל, שקורין אשייל"א בלע"ז. ולא נראה, שהרי בברייתא בגמרא תני: "עד האציל", ואי אפשר שהוא אשייל"א — דאיתא בפרק ב' דזבחים (דף יח:): "ולא יחגרו ביזע" — שלא היו חוגרים במקום זיעה: לא למטה ממתניהם, ולא למעלה מאציליהם (ולא תחת אצילי) [אלא כנגד אצילי] ידיהם. ואי אמרת דהוא אשייל"א — אדרבה, שם הוא מקום זיעה! לכך פירש ר"י, דהוא שקורין קוד"א. ובמנחות (דף לז. ושם) ובזבחים (דף יט.) הארכתי:
Tosafot on Arakhin 19a:5:1.english: "His elbow" - Rashi explained [it as the] atzil, which is called aissele in Old French [i.e., armpit]. And [this] does not appear [correct], for in a baraita in the Gemara it teaches: "Up to the atzil", and it is impossible that it is [the] aissele — as it is stated in the second chapter of Zevachim (18b): "They shall not gird themselves with sweat" [Ezekiel 44:18] — that they would not gird [their belts] in a place of sweat: neither below their loins, nor above their atzilim, (nor beneath the atzilim of) [rather opposite the atzilim of] their arms. And if you say that it is [the] aissele — on the contrary, that is [the very] place of sweat! Therefore, the Ri explained that it is what is called coude [in Old French, i.e., the elbow]. And in Menachot (37a and there) and in Zevachim (19a), I have elaborated.

Tosafot on Arakhin 19a:8:1.hebrew: דבתר דשקלי שדו תרי תלתא - וא"ת: בכל מקום נמי היו מעריכין יותר מן המשקל, כדמוכח בבבא בתרא פרק המוכר את הספינה (בבא בתרא דף פח:)), והיכי ס"ד דבטלה תורת משקל? וי"ל, דהכי פירוש: דהכא באתרא דשקלי, שדו תרי תילתי יותר מן הכרע; הלכך סלקא דעתך דבטלה, כיון שנותן יותר מכדין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 19a:8:1.english: "Where after they weigh, they throw in two [or] three" - And if you say: Everywhere, too, they would tip the scale [or: add an overweight] beyond the [exact] weight, as is proven in Bava Batra, in the chapter [entitled] "HaMokher Et HaSefinah" (88b); and [if so,] how could it enter your mind that the status of weight was nullified? And one can say that this is the explanation: Here, in the place where they weigh, they throw in two [or] three [onions, or: two-thirds] more than the tipping of the scale; therefore, it could enter your mind that [the status of weight] was nullified, since he gives more than what the law requires.
